subject: GFH: SKU floor protection + marketplace/private-offer routing and reseller margin
messages:
From: Elena Marten <elena@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: Marketplace pricing constraints + private offer ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the intro — quick ask from procurement as we move toward an internal approval: we need clarity on how a private offer will appear on AWS/GCP marketplaces with respect to list-price floors and whether that will affect our reseller margin structure. Two concrete items: 1) when Redwood issues a private offer (AWS/GCP), does the marketplace listing still show a list price that conflicts with an internal negotiated floor? 2) We have an incumbent reseller that expects a 20% net margin post-credits; can you confirm whether marketplace pass-throughs / credits will change their net?

I attached a draft PO and a simple pricing matrix. Can you and your finance/marketplace folks advise on: SKU mapping (so we can align PO line items to marketplace SKUs), a proposed channel margin split, and any constraints/flags procurement should include in the PO (e.g., list-price hold harmless, metadata showing private pricing)?

Appreciate quick guidance — we are aiming to finalize terms the week of May 22.

Best,
Elena
Elena Marten
Director, Procurement
Greenfield Health

Attachments: GFH_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 248 KB); GFH_PRICING_MATRIX.xlsx (XLSX, 92 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Marten <elena@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Marketplace pricing constraints + private offer ask

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the PO draft. Looping in Laura (deal ops) and Soojin (marketplace) — brief summary and next steps below.

High level answers up front:
- Private offers: on AWS/GCP the private-offer transaction is tied to a marketplace SKU/version, and systems typically still show a public list price. However, the private pricing is applied at procurement/checkout and is not visible to end-users in the invoice line if you select a private pricing workflow. We can add contractual language to the PO to ensure the list-price floor does not get surfaced in ways that cause downstream reseller adjustment requests.
- Reseller margin: credits and marketplace pass-throughs can reflow margin if the reseller invoices based on gross list price. We recommend structuring the reseller arrangement so they invoice net (post-private-offer price), or include an explicit pass-through credit clause.

What I will do now:
1) Laura — can you produce a SKU-to-PO-line mapping and a suggested margin waterfall (2-3 scenarios: conservative, standard, aggressive)?
2) Soojin — please confirm any marketplace constraints (AWS vs. GCP differences) for list-price metadata and whether we can add a hidden metadata flag or invoice annotation for reseller reconciliation.
3) Elena — if you can confirm the reseller entity (name and invoicing flow), we will incorporate an explicit clause for net invoicing or a hold-harmless credit step.

Attaching our private-offer guidelines and a short pricing template for your procurement team.

Thanks — will follow up with the mapping by EOD Monday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kar thik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Guidelines.pdf (PDF, 160 KB)

From: Elena Marten <elena@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Marketplace pricing constraints + private offer ask

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications from procurement:
- Reseller is HealthChannel LLC (VAT/Tax treated as reseller; they will invoice Greenfield and expect a 20% net margin after any credits).
- We prefer the reseller to invoice net if possible. If Redwood requires gross invoicing via marketplace mechanics, we will need a clear reconciliation mechanism.

One additional ask: can you confirm whether a private offer will block marketplace discounts/promotions so our negotiated floor isn't inadvertently impacted by subsequent public promotions?

I've attached an updated PO with the reseller legal name.

Best,
Elena

Attachments: GFH_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (updated)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Marten <elena@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Marketplace pricing constraints + private offer ask

Elena — thanks, Laura (Redwood deal ops) here — attaching the SKU mapping and three margin waterfall scenarios as discussed. Summary below (tl;dr):

1) SKU mapping: we mapped your PO line items to three marketplace SKUs (AWS-MI-RED-BASE, AWS-MI-RED-PREM, GCP-RED-ENTERPRISE). See attached GFH_PRICING_MATRIX.xlsx for line-by-line.

2) Private-offer visibility & promotions: private offers bind specific customer subscriptions and pricing at the time of the PO/checkout. Public promotions run separately; they will not retroactively change an executed private offer price. That said, marketplace metering and public promotions can affect perceived list-price if your reseller references historical public discounts — we recommend adding a PO clause: "Private-offer prices govern; public promotions do not alter negotiated private pricing or reseller margins."

3) Reseller margin & invoicing options (recommended):
   - Option A (preferred): Reseller invoices Greenfield net of private-offer price. Redwood invoices marketplace/MP as required; Redwood issues a pass-through confirmation to HealthChannel for reconciliation.
   - Option B (if marketplace gross invoicing required): Reseller invoices gross; Redwood provides a monthly or quarterly automated credit file that HealthChannel applies so they net 20% per agreed formula.

4) Technical flag: AWS currently supports a private-offer metadata field (partner_reconciliation_id) that we can populate; GCP has a similar field but requires partner ops coordination. Soojin, please add details on the metadata/ops steps.

Next steps:
- Soojin: confirm ops steps & timing for metadata annotation and whether we need to engage aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com.
- Elena: please confirm whether HealthChannel will invoice net (Option A) or need the credit file (Option B).

Laura Bennett
Deal Operations
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: GFH_PRICING_MATRIX.xlsx (updated)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, Elena Marten <elena@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Marketplace pricing constraints + private offer ask

Elena / team — Soojin (marketplace ops) here. Quick ops note and timeline:

- AWS: we can create a private offer tied to the chosen SKUs and populate partner_reconciliation_id and negotiated_price metadata. Private offers do not get overwritten by subsequent public promotions. To ensure HealthChannel nets 20%, recommend Option A (reseller invoices net). If HealthChannel must invoice gross, we will schedule a monthly credit file export (CSV) and provide an invoice attachment pattern for HealthChannel to apply credits.
- GCP: similar capability but requires a short onboarding (typically 3 business days) to enable private offer metadata.
- Doc/links: see internal ops playbook attached. I will engage aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com to pre-warm the private-offer with partner_reconciliation_id and to validate we can include an invoice note that references the PO and Redwood reconciliation id.

Proposed timeline:
- May 22: confirm HealthChannel invoicing preference
- May 23: Redwood publishes private offer draft to AWS/GCP (ops prep)
- May 24-25: Marketplace ops validation and signoff
- May 26: DocuSign-ready contract with PO clause and reconciliation appendix

Ben — looped you for a quick tax check on reseller net vs. gross when crediting across marketplaces.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Guidelines.pdf (ops excerpt)
